title: Plain block comparison
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $B$ be a natural number, let $K$ be a proposition, and let $\sigma=(p,n,a,b,s,t,tmp,st,nx)$ be a nine-register state. Suppose $2|x|+2\le B$, every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, and $p\le |x|$. Assume that whenever the suffix of $x$ beginning at position $p$ is exactly the binary word for $tmp$, in the sense that $\operatorname{PlainAt}(x,p,\operatorname{bits}(tmp))$ holds, the program started at label $w0$ with $p=|x|$ and $tmp=0$ terminates within the register bound and has an accepting branch exactly when $K$ holds. Then the program started at label $ttt$ in state $\sigma$ terminates within the register bound and has an accepting branch exactly when both $\operatorname{PlainAt}(x,p,\operatorname{bits}(tmp))$ and $K$ hold.
hypotheses_covered: Every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
If $\operatorname{PlainAt}(x,p,\operatorname{bits}(tmp))$, the program at $w0$ with $p=|x|$ and $tmp=0$ has property $K$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $K$ a proposition, and $σ$ a register
configuration whose nine register values are all at most $B$. Suppose the input pointer
$p$ is at most $|x|$. If, whenever the segment of $x$ beginning at $p$ agrees with the
binary word for $\mathrm{tmp}$ and ends exactly at the end of $x$, the fixed program
started at its next stage with pointer $|x|$ and scratch register $0$ terminates within
the register bound and accepts exactly when $K$ holds, then starting at the plain-block
comparison stage with configuration $σ$ terminates within the register bound and accepts
exactly when both that segment condition and $K$ hold.
